Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:2:1.hebrew: ואי כורכמא דרישקא - לכך נקט כורכמא דרישקא, שמתקיים בקרקע ג' שנים, דהיינו שני - חזקה, ודרך להשהותו בקרקע כמו שיכול להתקיים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:2:1.english: "And if it was a saffron crocus" - The reason [the Gemara] specified the saffron crocus of Rishka is that it lasts in the ground for three years, which are the years of chazakah (presumptive ownership) - and it is customary to leave it in the ground for as long as it can survive.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:4:1.hebrew: אלא כדי שיהא באספמיא - דעד שם יש מהלך שנה, ויותר מכאן אין דרך להרחיק יותר מקרקעו; ואם הרחיק יותר — לא פלוג:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:4:1.english: Rather, [it is] so that he would be in Spain - For up to there is a journey of a year, and beyond this it is not the way [of people] to go farther away from their land; and if he did go farther, we do not distinguish [between cases] (lo plug).

Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:5:1.hebrew: מחאה שלא בפניו כו' - תימה: דבכל דוכתי נקט "מחאה", ואמאי לא נקט "חזקה"? "שלא בפניו הויא חזקה"! ויש לומר: לפי שהטעם תלוי במחאה ולא בחזקה, שאדם המחזיק בקרקעותיו של חבירו אית ליה קלא, שהוא חוקר ושואל על נכסיו; אבל המחאה אין לה קול כל כך, שאין המחזיק מחזר אם מוחה לו בעל קרקע. לפיכך אין חזקתו חזקה כשאין יכול לשמוע מחאתו, דמה יועיל שמיחה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 38a:5:1.english: "Protest not in his presence," etc. - This is surprising: everywhere [else] the Gemara uses the term "protest" (*mechaah*), so why did it not say "*chazakah*" (presumptive possession)? [After all, the Gemara says that] if it was not in his presence, it is [still] a valid *chazakah*! And one can answer: Because the reasoning depends on the protest and not on the *chazakah*. For a person who holds the land of his fellow has publicity (*kala*), since [the owner] investigates and asks about his property. But a protest does not have that much publicity, since the occupier does not go around checking whether the landowner is protesting against him. Therefore his *chazakah* is not a [valid] *chazakah* when he cannot hear the protest — for what good would it be that [the owner] protested?
